text:
monitoring-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for /streaming/generate across region us-west-2. p95 -> 820ms, p99 -> 2.6s over last 2m. Error rate steady. Possible streaming stalls. Auto-page: @alex.k(oncall) :rotating_light:

alex.k: I'm on it. paging @sasha for runtime assist. Starting quick checks. any customer impact yet?

sasha: joining. can someone grab the grafana link and correlation for deploys? I'll check KV cache evictions and kvstore latencies.

riley: I'm watching traces now. Getting increased tail on renderer RPCs around 13:40UTC. sending trace link: <https://grafana.redwood/trace/abc123|trace-abc123>

jamie: FYI just before 13:38UTC we had small rollout to prod of batching heuristics (rollout id: ro-612). Could correlate.

alex.k: good call. incident-bot, create incident INC-2026-0421 and add SRE/Runtime/Oncall.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0421 opened by alex.k. Severity: P2. Conference bridge: https://meet.redwood/INC-2026-0421

marta.cs: any customer-facing degradation? CS monitoring shows a handful of slow requests in a couple of top accounts but no 5xx. I'll prep comms if it keeps.

sasha: quick checks:
```bash
# check redis/kvcache evictions
redis-cli -h kvcache-usw INFO | egrep 'evicted_keys|used_memory'
# check batching queue length
kubectl -n inference exec -it pod/runtime-xx -- sh -c 'ps aux | grep batch'
```

riley: traces show long waits in `kv.lookup` and `batcher.enqueue` for some requests. p99 correlates with queue depth spikes. looks like a backlog on a small pool of runtime pods.

jamie: i can scale the batcher pool in the autoscaling group and roll back the batching-heuristics flag. which is faster? scaling pods now vs rollback config.

alex.k: scale first for quick mitigation, then rollback if not improved. sasha, can you confirm autoscaler functioning?

sasha: autoscaler responding but max surge is limited by reserved capacity on dedicated nodes. increasing replica count now.

eng-runtime: scaling replicas +3 for service/stream-batcher -> current 6 -> 9. Pushing immediately.

monitoring-bot: Action recorded: scaled stream-batcher replicas to 9. Re-evaluating latency in 60s.

riley: seeing initial improvement at 30s. p95 dropping to ~300ms, p99 ~900ms but tail still flapping for specific customer routes.

marta.cs: sharing list of affected customers to support: acme-corp, lumen-data. CS on standby.

jamie: rolling back batching heuristics flag (ro-612) on 2 pods to test impact. patch applied to canary-1 and canary-2.

alex.k: good. keep canary only for now.

sasha: KV cache metrics show transient spike in miss rate earlier, maybe due to recent model switch. verifying model versions pinned.

eng-runtime: found one pod with elevated GC and slow IO; restarting it now.

monitoring-bot: Pod runtime-xx restarted by eng-runtime. Observability: logs at https://logs.redwood/runtime-xx

riley: after scale + restart + canary rollback, p99 now ~480ms, p95 ~190ms across region. traces show backlog clearing. No increase in 5xx.

marta.cs: CS standing down from active comms but will monitor 15m.

alex.k: filing follow-up action items:
- (sasha) Investigate autoscaler limits and reserved nodes impact (due EOD)
- (jamie) Run postmortem for batcher heuristics rollout + tighter canary gating
- (riley) Pull trace samples for affected accounts and add to incident timeline
- (eng-runtime) Add better queue depth alerting

sasha: ack. I'll open PR for autoscaler tuning and schedule with infra.

jamie: writing postmortem draft now.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0421 marked MONITORED. Next update due in 15m.

alex.k: thanks all — leaving oncall in 15m. handing to @sasha for next shift. @sasha you ready?

sasha: taking handoff. docs updated in incident board. tag me if anything flares.

marta.cs: CS noted handoff. will notify enterprise accounts if any new slowness.

eng-runtime: keeping watch on replicas and GC, will report if p99 >1s.

monitoring-bot: Update check at +15m: p99 stable under 600ms for last 10m. No increase in errors.

alex.k: good wrap. closing active triage thread — incident remains in MONITORED state for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
